comments.author: pbronez
comments.why: Similar setup at CalTech with huge optics.
comments.text: The slowmo guys did a video about a similar setup at CalTech [VIDEO] It’s super cool that AlphaPhoenix is able to get comparable results on his garage. These academic versions use huge lab bench optic setups. They wind up with technically higher quality results, but AlphaPhonix’s video is more compelling.

comments.author: ranger_danger
comments.story: Femtosecond lasers create 3D midair plasma displays you can touch (2015)
comments.why: Filming light with femtosecond lasers and streak camera.
comments.text: You can also use femtosecond lasers and a streak camera to film the speed of light: [VIDEO] Maybe one day something like this can be used to have true light-field cameras without microlens arrays (like Lytro had).

comments.author: teleforce
comments.why: Shows lab using Windows 7 with state-of-the-art camera.
comments.text: Your story reminds me of this research lab with state-of-the-art 10 Trillion FPS camera. From the video they apparently are still using Windows 7 for the measurement set up [1]. They're publishing in Nature and most probably using Excel for some of their data processing workflow. My former research lab is, however, mainly using Igor Pro software running on Windows. It is waves based professional data processing software tool that has friendly GUI and intuitive table interfaces not unlike Excel but geared towards scientists and engineers [2]. [1]Filming the Speed of Light at 10 Trillion FPS: [VIDEO] [2]IGOR Pro: [LINK]
